For professors

A proposal for faculty review: nothing changes in your course until it’s agreed.
Questions: reply to the email, or write to languagelab-gvl@ung.edu.

What changes

Same TalkAbroad conversations. Students get short pages, instructions on GitHub, and an optional reflection generator. Workshops run in person when a campus can staff them, and online when lab assistants from Dahlonega and Gainesville share them. Click a tile to see why; click again to turn it back.

Behind the scenes

Before→After

Structure

  • LAB folderBefore: Separate requirement, task, contact and TalkAbroad pages→After: One LAB folder with a tabbed description
  • Shorter pagesBefore: Long lab pages with drop-downs→After: What to do, what to talk about, and your notes. The workshop has its own tab
  • InstructionsBefore: Pages stored in each D2L course→After: Lab pages on GitHub, linked from D2L

Vocabulary

  • Word listsBefore: A summary list that didn't match the book→After: The Top Hat chapter lists, plus the words the chapters and workshops use
  • Words removedBefore: Words that aren't in Top Hat, like l'aéroport and des gants→After: 44 words removed; words used in a chapter or workshop stay
  • Top Hat errorsBefore: Typos and wrong meanings, like décevoir, to deceive→After: 18 corrected on the lab pages, listed in the Top Hat corrections section
  • AudioBefore: No audio on the lists→After: Each word links to Forvo, with a ▶ button as a backup

Deadlines

  • Due timeBefore: Fridays at 3:00 PM→After: Fridays at 5:00 PM, as in SPAN 1001

Sections

  • In-person workshopsBefore: One regular setup→After: A Lab Assistant runs each workshop in person
  • Online workshopsBefore: Online labs with no matching pages→After: The same workshops, run online by lab assistants from Dahlonega and Gainesville
  • Summer workshops (pending)Before: No workshops→After: No workshops for now. Pending: confirm whether summer sections should add them

Lab 0

  • Guidelines QuizBefore: No quiz on the lab rules→After: A TalkAbroad quiz: booking, files, deadlines, rubric. Passing it unlocks the labs
  • TalkAbroad setupBefore: An announcement students may skip→After: Lab 0 instructions, confirmed by students in the quiz. Nothing to turn in
  • AccentsBefore: No help typing French→After: A keyboard guide for Windows and Mac, with three typed questions in the quiz

New

  • Reflection generatorBefore: Reflection prompts with no place to write→After: Optional page: notes and reflection for the lab, saved as a PDF to upload

Discrepancy fixes

  • Lab 5 titleBefore: Le grand repaso, which is Spanish→After: La grande révision
  • Lab 5 gradingBefore: A reflection sheet on one page; accuracy and vocabulary on another→After: Attendance and participation only, with no submission
  • DropboxesBefore: “One TalkAbroad dropbox” and “two separate dropbox links”→After: One dropbox per lab, for both files
  • RecordingBefore: “About 20 minutes” and “within one hour”→After: Usually about 20 minutes. After an hour, contact TalkAbroad
  • Download stepBefore: “Download your recording” appears twice→After: One download step
  • RubricBefore: “25 points for completion”→After: The TalkAbroad rubric, shown in the proposal

Behind the scenes

  • New GitHub repositoryBefore: Instructions copied into D2L→After: fren1002-instructions, with Gainesville and Dahlonega copies
  • Course copyBefore: Copying a course brings last semester's lab items→After: Leave the lab items out; the Lab sets up fresh ones

What stays the same

  • TalkAbroad conversations, with a preparation document and an mp3.
  • Wednesdays at 11:59 PM in summer.
  • The TalkAbroad rubric, 25 points per lab.

Student workflow

Students go from the announcement to one LAB folder, complete Lab 0 (TalkAbroad setup and the Guidelines Quiz), then work through the labs in order. Click a step to see its page.

Previews show the Gainesville copy. Each campus gets its own copy that shows only its own Language Lab contact.

Optional for students. They pick a lab, write their notes and reflection, save a PDF, and upload it to D2L. Nothing they type leaves their browser.

GitHub › reflection page

TalkAbroad rubric

The current rubric stays: five rows at 5 points each. Lab 5 is attendance and participation only.

Content / Engagement 5Comprehensibility / Language control 5Discourse level / Fluency 5Pronunciation 5Preparation 5

Content / Engagement 5 points

  1. Exceeds expectations5Fully prepared and on time; active; rarely needed prompting.
  2. Meets expectations4Mostly prepared and on time; active most of the time; occasional prompting.
  3. Approaches expectations3Somewhat prepared or late; prompted often; partner did a lot of the talking.
  4. Does not meet expectations1Little or no preparation; partner did most of the talking.

Comprehensibility / Language control 5 points

  1. Exceeds expectations5Understood without difficulty; no clarification; no English.
  2. Meets expectations4Understood with little difficulty; 1–2 clarifications; rarely English.
  3. Approaches expectations3Some difficulty; 3–4 clarifications; occasional English.
  4. Does not meet expectations1Great difficulty; several clarifications; frequent English.

Discourse level / Fluency 5 points

  1. Exceeds expectations5Complete sentences with linking words; natural flow; not read or rehearsed.
  2. Meets expectations4Almost always complete sentences; a few linking words and longer pauses.
  3. Approaches expectations3Mix of complete and incomplete sentences; longer pauses, partly read.
  4. Does not meet expectations1Mainly incomplete sentences; long pauses; read or heavily rehearsed.

Pronunciation 5 points

  1. Exceeds expectations5Most words accurate; errors don't impede communication.
  2. Meets expectations4Most words accurate, often with English interference; no breakdown.
  3. Approaches expectations3Strong English influence; needs a sympathetic listener.
  4. Does not meet expectations1Few words accurate; many unintelligible; listener struggles.

Preparation 5 points

  1. Exceeds expectations5All aspects of the prompt, with analysis and original ideas.
  2. Meets expectations4All or most aspects; some analysis, more retelling.
  3. Approaches expectations3A few aspects missing; little analysis.
  4. Does not meet expectations1Some aspects missing; simple retelling only.

Lab 5 isn't scored with this rubric: it's attendance and participation only.

    Copying your course to a new semester New

    When you copy last semester's course into the new one, leave the lab items out. The Language Lab sets up the LAB folder, its files and the dropboxes in every new course. Copying last semester's lab items creates duplicates and old dropboxes.

    1. In the new course: Course Admin › Import / Export / Copy Components › Copy Components from another Org Unit. Search for your old course, then choose Select Components.

    2. Choose components: set them as shown, then choose Continue.

    3. D2L then shows one page for each component you set to individual items. On each page, uncheck the lab items:

      1. Select Content Modules and Topics: Uncheck the LAB folder. Its name depends on the section type; uncheck whichever shows. Continue.

      2. Select Course Files: Uncheck the lab files folder, whichever shows. Continue.

      3. Assignments: Uncheck the lab dropboxes. Continue.

      4. Grades: Uncheck the Lab Assignments category. Its grade items uncheck with it. Continue.

      5. Quizzes: Uncheck the Guidelines Quiz. Continue.

    4. Finish the copy as usual.
